LESSON: TALK ABOUT

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Effective By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners listen to stories and ide
Topic 1.4: Talk about

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Talk about. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and 

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TALK ABOUT
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Talk about helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: TALK ABOUT
Study Talk about like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and 

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Talk about”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Talk about is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Talk about”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Talk about to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and .
3. Make one local Kenya example of Talk about from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Talk about: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Talk about?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Talk about means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate expressions to media, in groups, pairs, and whole class describe people, situations, and .

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
